first_impression.reaction: Googled 'honeymoon planning service' on the train because I can't face booking Bali flights, villas and a boat day on top of the wedding. The first sentence tells me what it is, and the takeaways are four short lines, so I kept going. I read the 'questions to ask' list properly, skimmed 'how it works' and the FAQ, and skipped most of the wedding and name change bit. Bookmarked for the questions list. Still no idea what it costs, and the FAQ that should tell me sidesteps it.

journey.quote: A honeymoon planning service is one person who plans and books your honeymoon for you: the flights, the stays, the days in between, all held in a single itinerary.
journey.reaction: First line answers my search. Exactly what I want on a phone.

journey.quote: Decide your dates, length, style and must-haves first, then ask any planner about fees, inclusions, terms, insurance, exchange rates and commissions.
journey.reaction: Short, scannable, tells me what to do next. I could stop here and still get something out of it.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: For a two-week honeymoon, that might be a long-haul flight, two or three stays, a private dinner, a boat for a day and the connections between them.
journey.reaction: Concrete. I can picture my own trip in that list.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.reaction: As a heading this tells me nothing when I'm scrolling. Is it step one? I only worked out it was a step from the line above it.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.
journey.reaction: That's the third time in a few lines I've read 'in writing'. I got it the first time. Starting to feel like it's repeating itself instead of telling me anything new.

journey.section: Planning the honeymoon alongside your wedding
journey.quote: Planning them as two separate projects means two sets of contacts, two sets of deadlines and two lots of quotes in foreign currencies to convert at the kitchen table.
journey.reaction: Fair point, the kitchen table line made me smile. That's literally us with SGD and IDR.

journey.quote: Born in Australia and married overseas? You will always need a name change certificate for your passport.
journey.reaction: Didn't come for this but it's useful and I wouldn't have known. A bit dense on a phone, though.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: These are worth asking whoever you speak to, including us. The answers should come back clearly, and in writing. The points below are general information as at November 2026.
journey.reaction: Dated and not pushy. That's the bit that makes me trust it's current.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: **Do you hold insolvency insurance?** Agent insolvency is commonly excluded from cancellation cover, and insolvency insurance is not compulsory for agents, so only some have it.
journey.reaction: Never would have thought to ask. Saving this list.

journey.quote: You can arrange it yourselves, or hand the planning and booking to a planner who books it on your behalf, so your evenings stay clear for the wedding.
journey.reaction: This FAQ just repeats the one above it. Doesn't add anything.

journey.quote: Work back from your dates rather than a rule.
journey.reaction: I wanted a rough number of months. It gives me a way of thinking instead. Reasonable, but I scrolled for it.

journey.quote: A fee only means something next to what it covers.
journey.reaction: Just tell me how much it costs. This is the question I'd most likely have Googled, and it's the one answer that dodges.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a honeymoon planner cost, and is it a flat fee or a percentage?
Can Wedded Wonderland plan a honeymoon for someone living in Singapore, not Australia, and would it quote in AUD or SGD?
If we're not doing a destination wedding, just the honeymoon, is that still a normal job for you?
Roughly how many months ahead should we start?

turn_offs_found.why: Heading doesn't match what I'm scanning for. It reads like a slogan, not a step. Something like 'Step 1: tell us what you want' would make the two-step process obvious on a phone.

turn_offs_found.quote: So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.
turn_offs_found.why: Repeats the sentence right before it. The 'in writing' point appears in the intro, takeaways, this section, the questions, the FAQ and the close. On a phone, repetition reads as filler.
Answer overlaps almost word for word with 'What does a honeymoon planning service do?'. One weak FAQ makes the others feel padded.

would_share_with: My fiance, for the 'questions to ask any planner' list
A friend getting married overseas next year, for the name change bit

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [speak with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planning-service&utm_content=closing) and tell us anything.
cta_reaction.why: The page was straight with me and the plugs were short, so I'd come back. But I came to understand the service, not hire one on the train, and without a ballpark cost or knowing if they work with people outside Australia I'm not clicking yet.

top_3_changes: Cut the repeated 'in writing' lines in 'How it works', especially 'So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.', so the section says each thing once.
Rename 'Tell us anything' to a plain step heading (for example 'Step 1: Tell us what you want') so the two-step process is clear when skimming.
Drop or replace the 'Who arranges the honeymoon?' FAQ, which repeats the first FAQ; a question that adds something new would earn its place.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone
No invented brand facts; missing info went to unanswered_questions
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection

Deferred business details (fee basis, commissions, who is on the ground, scale proof, real honeymoons, perks, Wedded Privileges) not treated as must-fix; cost question kept in unanswered_questions and CTA reaction only

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Framed as an Australian living in Singapore planning a Bali wedding and honeymoon (consistent with earlier Priya readings).
